text: (a) Write the molecular formula of the following carbon compounds: (i) Methane (ii) Propane. (b) Carbon compounds have low melting and boiling points. Why? (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Methane: CH4; Propane: C3H8. (b) Most carbon compounds are covalent (molecular) compounds, so the intermolecular forces of attraction between their molecules are weak (van der Waals forces), not strong forces like in ionic compounds. Only a small amount of energy is needed to overcome these weak forces, so carbon compounds have low melting and boiling points.
keyPoints: Methane = CH4, Propane = C3H8
Carbon compounds are largely covalent/molecular, not ionic
Weak intermolecular (van der Waals) forces need little energy to break

text: The electrons in the atoms of two elements X and Y are distributed in three shells having 1 and 7 electrons respectively in their outermost shells. (a) Write the group numbers of these elements in the Modern Periodic Table. (b) Write the molecular formula of the compound formed when X and Y combine with each other. (c) Which of the two is electropositive? (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: X has configuration 2,8,1 (atomic number 11, sodium) so it belongs to Group 1. Y has configuration 2,8,7 (atomic number 17, chlorine) so it belongs to Group 17. (b) X and Y combine by transfer of the one outer electron of X to Y, forming the ionic compound NaCl. (c) X (sodium) is electropositive since it loses an electron to form a positive ion.
keyPoints: Configuration 2,8,1 → Group 1; configuration 2,8,7 → Group 17
Compound formed: NaCl
X (the Group 1 element) is electropositive

text: (a) Which of the following flowers will have higher possibility of self-pollination? Mustard, Papaya, Watermelon, Hibiscus. (b) List the two reproductive parts of a bisexual flower. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Mustard, because it is a bisexual flower in which the anther and stigma are close together and mature around the same time, favouring self-pollination; Papaya and Watermelon have unisexual flowers (separate male and female flowers), so they cannot self-pollinate. (b) The two reproductive parts of a bisexual flower are the stamen (androecium, the male part that produces pollen) and the pistil/carpel (gynoecium, the female part containing the ovary, style and stigma).
keyPoints: Mustard is bisexual with anther and stigma close together — self-pollination possible
Papaya and Watermelon are unisexual, so self-pollination is not possible
Reproductive parts: stamen (male) and pistil/carpel (female)

text: Which one of the two multicellular organisms, Spirogyra and Planaria, reproduces by regeneration and why? Give an example of any other organism which can also reproduce by the same process. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: Planaria reproduces by regeneration: if its body is cut into pieces, each piece contains cells that can divide repeatedly and differentiate into all the different cell types needed, so each piece grows into a complete new organism. (Spirogyra instead reproduces by fragmentation, simply breaking into pieces that each grow, without this specialised regenerative process.) Hydra is another organism that reproduces by regeneration.
keyPoints: Planaria reproduces by regeneration
Cells in the body fragment divide and differentiate to rebuild the whole organism
Another example: Hydra

text: What is variation? List two main reasons that may lead to variation in a population. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: Variation is the difference in characters/traits seen among individuals of the same species/population. Two main reasons for variation: (i) inaccuracies (mutations) that occur while copying DNA during reproduction; (ii) in sexual reproduction, DNA from two parents combines and reshuffles (recombination), producing offspring with new combinations of traits.
keyPoints: Variation = differences in traits among individuals of a population
Reason 1: errors/mutations during DNA copying
Reason 2: recombination of DNA from two parents in sexual reproduction

text: (a) Name and state the rule that determines the direction of force experienced by a current-carrying straight conductor placed in a uniform magnetic field which is perpendicular to it. (b) An alpha particle, while passing through a magnetic field, gets deflected towards north. In which direction will an electron be deflected when it passes through the same magnetic field? (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand mutually perpendicular to each other; if the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, then the thumb points in the direction of the force (motion) on the conductor. (b) An alpha particle is positively charged and an electron is negatively charged, so the force on the electron in the same field (moving the same way) is in the opposite direction — the electron will be deflected towards the south.
keyPoints: Rule: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule
Thumb = force, forefinger = field, middle finger = current
Opposite charge (electron vs alpha particle) means the deflection is reversed — south

text: What is ozone? How is it formed in the upper layers of the atmosphere? How does ozone affect our ecosystem? (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: Ozone (O3) is a molecule made of three oxygen atoms. In the upper atmosphere (stratosphere), high-energy ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun splits some oxygen molecules (O2) into free oxygen atoms, which then combine with other O2 molecules to form ozone (O3). The ozone layer absorbs most of the harmful UV radiation from the sun, shielding living organisms on Earth from its damaging effects (such as skin cancer and damage to DNA), so it protects the ecosystem.
keyPoints: Ozone = O3, three oxygen atoms
Formed when UV radiation splits O2 into O atoms, which combine with O2 to form O3
Ozone layer absorbs harmful UV radiation, protecting living organisms

text: (a) List two advantages of adopting the atomic number of an element as the basis of classifying elements in the Modern Periodic Table. (b) Write the electronic configurations of the elements X (atomic number 13) and Y (atomic number 20). (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Two advantages: (i) Classifying by atomic number correctly explains the periodicity of properties, since elements with the same number of valence electrons (which atomic number determines) recur periodically — this fixed anomalies of Mendeleev's atomic-mass-based table, such as the correct ordering of pairs like cobalt-nickel or argon-potassium. (ii) Atomic number equals the number of protons/electrons, which directly determines an element's electronic configuration and hence its chemical properties, making the classification more scientifically sound and predictive. (b) X (atomic number 13): electronic configuration 2, 8, 3 (aluminium). Y (atomic number 20): electronic configuration 2, 8, 8, 2 (calcium).
keyPoints: Atomic number fixes anomalies like Co-Ni, Ar-K ordering seen with atomic mass
Atomic number = number of electrons, which fixes electronic configuration and properties

text: Draw two different possible structures of a saturated hydrocarbon having four carbon atoms in its molecule. What are these two structures of the hydrocarbon having the same molecular formula called? Write the molecular formula and the common name of this compound. Also write the molecular formula of its alkyne. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: The saturated hydrocarbon with four carbon atoms is butane, C4H10. Its two structures are: n-butane, a straight chain, CH3-CH2-CH2-CH3; and isobutane (2-methylpropane), a branched chain, CH3-CH(CH3)-CH3. Structures with the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms are called isomers (chain isomers). Molecular formula: C4H10; common name: butane. The corresponding alkyne (butyne) has molecular formula C4H6.
keyPoints: Straight-chain n-butane: CH3-CH2-CH2-CH3; branched isobutane: CH3-CH(CH3)-CH3
Same molecular formula, different structure → called isomers
Molecular formula C4H10, common name butane; its alkyne (butyne) is C4H6

text: (a) Mention one function each of the following organs in the human male reproductive system: (i) Testis (ii) Scrotum (iii) Vas deferens (iv) Prostate gland. (b) Name the type of germ cell which (i) is motile, and (ii) stores food. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) (i) Testis: produces sperm (male gametes) and the hormone testosterone. (ii) Scrotum: a pouch that keeps the testes outside the abdominal cavity at a lower temperature suitable for sperm production. (iii) Vas deferens: carries sperm from the testis to the urethra. (iv) Prostate gland: secretes fluid that, along with secretions of other glands, forms the seminal fluid that nourishes and helps transport sperm. (b) (i) The sperm (male gamete) is motile, using its tail to swim. (ii) The ovum/egg (female gamete) stores food (nutrients) for the early development of the embryo.
keyPoints: Testis: produces sperm and testosterone; scrotum: keeps testes cool; vas deferens: carries sperm; prostate: adds seminal fluid
Motile germ cell: sperm
Food-storing germ cell: ovum/egg

text: (a) Define electric power and write its SI unit. (b) Two bulbs rated 100 W; 220 V and 60 W; 220 V are connected in parallel to an electric mains of 220 V. Find the current drawn by the bulbs from the mains. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Electric power is the rate at which electrical energy is consumed (or work is done) in a circuit: P = W/t = VI = I²R = V²/R. Its SI unit is the watt (W). (b) In parallel, both bulbs get the full mains voltage of 220 V, so together they consume 100 W + 60 W = 160 W. Total current drawn = P/V = 160/220 ≈ 0.73 A.
keyPoints: Electric power = rate of consumption of electrical energy; P = VI; SI unit is watt
In parallel, total power = sum of individual powers = 160 W
Current from mains = P/V = 160/220 ≈ 0.73 A

text: (a) Name the group of organisms which form the first trophic level of all food chains. Why are they called so? (b) Why are human beings most adversely affected by bio-magnification? (c) State one ill-effect of the absence of decomposers from a natural ecosystem. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Producers (autotrophs, e.g. green plants) form the first trophic level, because they make their own food through photosynthesis and so are the ultimate source of energy for every food chain. (b) Humans are most adversely affected by bio-magnification because they usually occupy the topmost trophic level in food chains, so harmful chemicals (like pesticides) that increase in concentration at each successive trophic level reach their highest concentration by the time they reach humans. (c) Without decomposers, dead remains and waste would not be broken down, so nutrients would never be recycled back into the soil/ecosystem, disrupting the nutrient cycle.
keyPoints: Producers are the first trophic level — they make their own food via photosynthesis
Humans are at the top of most food chains, so bio-magnified toxins reach their highest concentration in humans
Without decomposers, dead matter piles up and nutrients are not recycled

text: What is the function of the diaphragm in the human respiratory system? Where is it present in the human body? (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: The diaphragm is a sheet of muscle that helps change the volume of the chest (thoracic) cavity during breathing: it contracts and flattens during inhalation, expanding the chest cavity so air is drawn into the lungs, and it relaxes and domes upward during exhalation, pushing air out. It is present at the base of the thoracic (chest) cavity, separating it from the abdominal cavity.
keyPoints: Diaphragm changes the volume of the chest cavity to draw air in/push air out
Contracts and flattens during inhalation; relaxes/domes up during exhalation
Located at the base of the chest cavity, between chest and abdomen

text: State two differences between the act of chewing food and salivation on sight of food. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: Chewing is a voluntary, mechanical action — consciously controlled by the jaw muscles to physically break food into smaller pieces. Salivation on sight of food is an involuntary reflex action — it is triggered automatically by the brain/nervous system (even before food is in the mouth) and results in the chemical secretion of saliva by the salivary glands, not a mechanical breakdown.
keyPoints: Chewing = voluntary, mechanical breakdown of food by jaw muscles/teeth
Salivation on sight of food = involuntary reflex, triggered by the brain before food is even eaten
One is a physical action, the other is a glandular secretion response

text: OR: State two differences between pollination and fertilization. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a flower, an external process occurring on the flower itself. Fertilization is the fusion of the male gamete (carried down the pollen tube) with the female gamete (egg cell) inside the ovule, an internal process that happens within the ovary, and it can only occur after pollination has taken place.
keyPoints: Pollination: transfer of pollen from anther to stigma (external, on the flower)
Fertilization: fusion of male and female gametes inside the ovule (internal, in the ovary)
Fertilization always occurs after pollination

text: Given below is a pyramid showing various trophic levels in an ecosystem: (i) Producers (ii) Primary consumers (iii) Secondary consumers (iv) Tertiary consumers. (a) From the organisms listed below, identify which one is to be placed at which trophic level: Deer, Grass, Lion, Snake, Rabbit. (b) Discuss the reason why primary consumers will have more energy as compared to secondary consumers. (c) Why is the base of the pyramid broad? (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Grass — producer (level i); Deer and Rabbit — primary consumers (level ii, herbivores that eat grass); Snake — secondary consumer (level iii, eats primary consumers like the rabbit); Lion — tertiary consumer (level iv, apex predator). (b) At each trophic level only about 10% of the energy is passed on to the next level (the rest is lost as heat, used in respiration, or in body parts not eaten); since primary consumers are one level below secondary consumers, they retain more of the original energy captured by producers. (c) The base of the pyramid is broad because producers have the greatest energy/biomass/numbers, and both energy and numbers decrease sharply at each successive trophic level (only about 10% is transferred upward), so the pyramid narrows towards the top.
keyPoints: Grass = producer; Deer & Rabbit = primary consumers; Snake = secondary consumer; Lion = tertiary consumer
Only ~10% of energy passes to the next trophic level, so primary consumers retain more energy than secondary consumers
Base is broad because producers have the most energy/biomass, which shrinks at each higher level

text: Give differences between the following: (a) Nephron and neuron (b) Sensory nerve and motor nerve (c) Consumers and decomposers. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) A nephron is the structural and functional unit of the kidney, responsible for filtering blood and forming urine (part of the excretory system); a neuron is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system, responsible for conducting electrical nerve impulses. (b) Sensory nerves carry impulses from sense organs/receptors to the brain or spinal cord (afferent); motor nerves carry impulses from the brain or spinal cord to muscles or glands (efferent). (c) Consumers depend on other organisms (producers or other consumers) for food and obtain organic matter directly; decomposers break down dead and decaying organic matter into simpler substances, releasing nutrients back into the environment.
keyPoints: Nephron = unit of the kidney (excretion); neuron = unit of the nervous system (impulse conduction)
Sensory nerves carry impulses TO the brain/spinal cord; motor nerves carry impulses FROM them
Consumers eat other organisms for food; decomposers break down dead matter and recycle nutrients

text: Give reasons for the following: (a) Covalent compounds are poor conductors of electricity. (b) Soap does not form lather in hard water. (c) Carbon shows catenation but silicon does not. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Covalent compounds do not form ions — their molecules are electrically neutral, with electrons tightly shared between the bonded atoms, so there are no free-moving charged particles (ions or free electrons) to carry an electric current. (b) Hard water contains dissolved calcium and magnesium salts (Ca2+, Mg2+ ions); these ions react with soap to form an insoluble precipitate (scum), so the soap gets used up in this reaction instead of producing lather. (c) Carbon atoms are small, forming strong and stable C-C bonds, which allows carbon to link with itself extensively (catenation); silicon atoms are larger, so Si-Si bonds are much weaker and less stable, so silicon shows very limited catenation.
keyPoints: Covalent compounds have no free ions/electrons to carry current
Ca2+/Mg2+ in hard water react with soap to form insoluble scum instead of lather
Small carbon atoms form strong stable C-C bonds (catenation); silicon's larger atoms form weak Si-Si bonds

text: Write chemical equations for the following: (a) Oxidation of ethanol by acidified K2Cr2O7. (b) Hydrogenation of ethene. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) CH3CH2OH + 2[O] --(acidified K2Cr2O7, heat)--> CH3COOH + H2O (ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid). (b) CH2=CH2 + H2 --(Ni catalyst)--> CH3-CH3 (ethene is hydrogenated to ethane).
keyPoints: Ethanol + acidified K2Cr2O7 (oxidising agent) → ethanoic acid (acetic acid) + water
Ethene + H2 in presence of Ni catalyst → ethane
Both are examples of addition/oxidation reactions in carbon compounds

text: The resistance of a wire of radius 0.01 cm and length 1.0 cm is 7 Ω. Calculate its resistivity. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: Radius r = 0.01 cm = 1 x 10⁻⁴ m, so cross-section area A = πr² = π x (1 x 10⁻⁴)² ≈ 3.14 x 10⁻⁸ m². Length L = 1.0 cm = 1 x 10⁻² m. Using R = ρL/A, resistivity ρ = RA/L = (7 x 3.14 x 10⁻⁸) / (1 x 10⁻²) ≈ 2.2 x 10⁻⁵ Ω m.
keyPoints: Convert radius and length to metres, find area A = πr²
Use R = ρL/A, rearranged to ρ = RA/L
Resistivity ≈ 2.2 x 10⁻⁵ Ω m

text: OR: An electric heater is rated 220 V; 11 A. Calculate the power consumed if the heater is operated at 200 V. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: The heater's resistance (assumed constant) is R = V/I = 220/11 = 20 Ω. When operated at 200 V, power consumed P = V²/R = 200²/20 = 40000/20 = 2000 W.
keyPoints: Find resistance from rated values: R = V/I = 220/11 = 20 Ω
Resistance stays the same when the operating voltage changes
Power at 200 V: P = V²/R = 200²/20 = 2000 W

text: The pattern of magnetic field due to a current-carrying wire depends upon the shape made by that wire. Justify. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: A straight current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field in the form of concentric circles around it (direction given by the right-hand thumb rule). When the wire is bent into a circular loop, the field contributions from all parts of the loop add up (superpose); near the centre of the loop they all point the same way, so the field there is nearly straight and stronger than around a straight wire. In a solenoid (many circular turns of wire), the fields of all the turns add up along the axis, producing a strong, uniform field inside that resembles the field of a bar magnet. Since the field at any point is the combined effect of the current in every part of the wire, changing the wire's shape changes how those contributions add up, so the overall field pattern depends on the shape of the conductor.
keyPoints: Straight wire: concentric circular field lines around it
Circular loop: field contributions add up, becoming nearly straight/uniform near the centre
Solenoid: fields of many loops add along the axis, giving a strong uniform field like a bar magnet
